newsitem.title: USA: More work needed for Hebron deal, U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: More work needed for Hebron deal, U.S. says.

text.p: Israel and the Palestinians need to make "additional movement" before they can strike a deal on the West Bank town of Hebron, the U.S. State Department said on Monday.

"Despite the good work by (U.S. mediator) Dennis Ross today, there is no deal yet and there remains the need for additonal movement and additional work by both the Israelis and Palestinians before there can be a deal," spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
Burns said, however, that thanks to the weekend intervention of King Hussein of Jordan "a lot of progress" had been made on non-Hebron issues tied to an agreement.

An Israeli handover of 80 percent of Hebron has seemed within reach many times in recent months but concerns for the security of the West Bank town's 400 Jews and 100,000 Arabs -- along with other issues -- have delayed an agreement.
In Israel, Ross was meeting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at his office in parliament before Israeli and Palestinian negotiators reconvened in Jerusalem from a four-hour recess.

Secretary of State Warren Christopher, who asked Ross to call off a plan to return to the United States Sunday evening, would "evaluate on a day-by-day basis" how long Ross should stay in the region, Burns said.
